messages:
ana: Quick heads-up — ran a microingest perf audit after the kernel-routing change. Seeing a p95 tail increase (~8-12%) for short streaming requests over HTTP/gRPC. Root cause not obvious yet, posting top-line traces. Looking for quick triage.

mike: Can you share the exact workload you used? sample rate, tokens per req, parallelism?

ana: (typo) sorry — ana: workload: 1k qps, 128-token avg, concurrent 80, two regions. Both http1 streaming and grpc streaming show the same pattern.

devon: Did the kernel picker change land with any new batching hints? I remember the PR added a small threshold tweak for mini-batches.

ana: yes — kernel-routing now prefers small-kernel for sequences <96 unless kv-cache hit rate > 0.7. Might be oscillation with kv hit heuristics.

sarah: If KV hit detection is noisy, requests could flip between kernels mid-stream. That would add parse/tokenization overhead. Did you see increased tokenizer sys CPU?

kelsey: Posting a quick flame summary I pulled: 

```
parse_request         42.1%
tokenizer             21.3%
grpc_write             8.7%
http_parser            6.2%
kv_cache_lookup        4.1%
other                 17.6%
```

kelsey: This was from host worker 12 during a synthetic run. Tokenizer and parse_request jumped ~+20% vs baseline.

ana: Interesting — kv_cache_lookup isn't the biggest CPU consumer but misses could cause extra work upstream. Any correlation with bursty prefix misses?

mike: Could be batching heuristics: if small-kernel path reduces continuous batching window, throughput drops and more parse cycles per token happen. We should check batching window histograms.

devon: I just checked traces — there are a lot more kernel-switch events in the hot path. Looks like for a subset of requests the router flips after first chunk because kv hit probability estimate updates.

perf-bot: Regression alert: 6234567000..6234567800 - host-ingress: p95 tail +9.4% (deploy 2026-03-22T10:12Z). See run: https://perf.redwood.local/runs/6234

sarah: If switching mid-stream is the issue we have two mitigation options: 1) pin kernel per-request at ingress based on initial estimate, or 2) delay switching until chunk boundary where aggregator has kvcache stability. Option 1 is simpler for canary.

kelsey: Quick repro command: `make perf-run WORKERS=80 QPS=1000 TOKENS=128 -run microingest-kernel-test` — includes http/grpc toggles.

mike: For a fast mitigation I'm for pinning per-request at ingress for 1.2 release, then follow-up with more robust heuristics to avoid oscillation.

devon: I'll open a small PR to set request-scoped kernel_hint on ingress path and add a metric `kernel_switches/req`. Will run canary tomorrow.

ana: thanks. assigning: devon -> PR + canary, kelsey -> reproduce script & flame, sarah -> design note for delayed switch, mike -> rollout plan.

sarah: one more ask — capture per-chunk kv hit trace (just sample 1%) so we can validate hit-rate estimator. :eyes:

kelsey: on it. I'll push trace collection and drop samples into the perf bucket.

ana: great. if we get canary green we can revert the heuristic tweak or make it stable. Appreciate the quick responses :thumbsup:
